title: Dealing with market-saturation in a post-AI game landscape
author: WonderfulMacaroon124
selftext:
**Disclaimer: This isn't an anti-ai post.**

So with AI tools, the barrier of entry to making games is massively lower. It is drastically more feasible to make complex things. I've seen the argument "it doesn't matter how good AI is, you still need a good developer to make good games". Whether this is true, it doesn't negate how much easier AI makes things. On Steam and itch, the number of new games has swelled in recent months and continues to climb.

Getting people to notice anything you make is already a huge challenge. It doesn't take a genius to figure that this problem will basically be on steroids soon.

So, with this in mind, what do you think the future looks like? As a developer, how do you plan to deal with visibility? Surely as developers who have been using AI, this has crossed your mind?

comments.author: MrNotmark
comments.body:
More supply and same demand always equals more competition, there will be much more competition, more people will expect quality products and simple clones will lose their appeal. 

It's simple. Now that everyone can make AI games you have to stand out and not be like the crowd that's it.

comments.author: speaks-with-stone
comments.body: Curation. The future is curation. The question is how to get to curators, and the answer is same old - nag. The more things change, the more they stay the same.

replies.author: Historical_Lock378
replies.body:
Curation still requires a brain. Look at art museums. Art curation has been a thing ever since people have been willing to pay for it. I dont think anti-AIers will ever look at it as Curation though

They will always see it as a evil which i find hilarious.

replies.author: somekindatog
replies.body: Also hyperniche and hyper local. You can make games for a very small audience and reach them

comments.author: anon999387
comments.body: Once it becomes more widely known how easily some of these games are being made, and in an almost automated fashion, the relative value of them will make $10 games becoming $1 games.

replies.author: Historical_Lock378
replies.body:
Not exactly true.. People dont care how easily something is made they are willing to pay for something if they think they will enjoy it enough to be willing to pay for it.

It goes the same with music or any other form of art. There are plenty of songs out their that in theory required less talent or work to put together but people still listened or paid for it.

Hard & long work in art doesn't guarantee a high price if anything it might make the artist re-think their approach that maybe there is a easier way and 9/10 when we are talking about humans they will choose the path of least resistance. Especially if the outcome is either same, better, more cost effective or less timely..

replies.author: anon999387
replies.body: You are arguing against a point I didn't make. I'm not saying a game's value is determined by how much work went into it, I'm saying that as ai hugely lowers the cost and difficulty of producing games, the supply of comparable games will increase. When people have more alternatives competing for their attention/money, that put a downward pressure on prices even if the quality remains the same.

replies.author: Historical_Lock378
replies.body:
But you literally said

"Once it becomes more widely known how EASILY some of these games are being made, and in an almost automated fashion"

in conjunction with

"The relative value of them will make $10 games becoming $1 games"

You are literally saying games that are made easier are less of a value.

I am very literally arguing against the point you were trying to make. It's obvious lol.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
yes, visibility is going to be a problem. And I suspect platforms are going to start getting much more scrutinizing about what gets in, or if they don't want to bother, they'll just raise the paywall barrier to get in 

. People felt $100 and public embarrassment was worth showing their whole ass for Next Fest, so Steam will probably kick up the cost of admission. it's the easiest way to deter morons and get-rich-quick operations; $100 is something you can wager without a lot of thought. Tack on another zero, and suddenly that calculation changes 

So I think we'll be faced with a two-pronged problem going forward due to the morons and get-rich-quickers that are abusing the technology and stores: it will become more expensive to publish and harder / more expensive to promote your game. This will choke out the river of shit currently flowing into digital stores, but will also mean - for a lot of people that aren't abusing the system - you'll be left out of the club too. 

It's shitty, but it is what it is.

comments.author: yojojomomo
comments.body: I expect quality for games will have to improve to stand out

replies.author: Historical_Lock378
replies.body: I don't think anyone will complain about this. This is actually a super good thing.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: Either the quality has to be so good or it will drown with all the other clones.

comments.author: Material-Watercress1
comments.body: Marketing will become even more important to be able to stand out from the rest. The storefronts are incapable of driving traffic to your game so it will need to come externally via socials

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
One of the things ive noticed is, i don’t buy games anymore. I used to buy an early access or indie game like every month or so on a steam sale. Now i open the store and say, actually, i’d rather just work on mine. 

Getting a game to playtest used to be a huge hurdle, now it’s relatively easy. I think it’s highly probable that games become essentially free and not full of hidden costs free but legit free cuz it’s a hobby and ai coded it and it didn’t take that much time and who cares if i give it away.

comments.author: situ139
comments.body:
Most of the stuff released is slop. I expect the over quality for games to increase, and most of these slop developers will quit after a year. But with that said you will still have more developer overall, but quality is going to be even more important.

Idk if anyone has ever noticed but able to make something that looks like a game and making something that is actually fun to play, is worlds apart.

comments.author: haven_fr
comments.body: just make a good human designed and polished game.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
i love it since I get to make great games now. i honestly dont care about other devs or how many there are since i know im at the top with whatever i finish as a game, so bring 10.000 games a month or more, its still done by the usual human who is nothing compared to me.

-> is my mindset. you asked.

also im hell of an extroverted person, marketing was always one of my strongest points so no worries there.

comments.author: Xanma_6aki
comments.body: If the ai bubble pops it will be too expensive for people to put out slop games and the market will heal
